## Overview

Enable existing native 8/16/32-head kernels in SM90 BF16 sparse FlashMLA for sufficiently large query batches, avoiding unnecessary computation from padding heads to 64.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61615

## Claims

- Reduce head-padding overhead in the BF16 sparse attention path.
- Preserve the padded path for small query batches, where native small-head kernels can be slower.
- Improve output throughput by 10.0% in the recorded GLM-5.3-Flash serving benchmark.

## Validation

Serving benchmark: GLM-5.3-Flash, TP4 with EP, BF16 KV cache, 16,384 input tokens, 512 output tokens, 128 requests, concurrency 32.

| Metric | main | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput | 258.99 tok/s | 284.97 tok/s | +10.0% |
| Mean TTFT | 11,161.42 ms | 9,981.46 ms | −10.6% |
| Mean TPOT | 101.74 ms | 92.77 ms | −8.8% |
| Mean end-to-end latency | 63,150.57 ms | 57,385.93 ms | −9.1% |

```
vllm serve \                                                   
  zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \                                                                            
  --host 127.0.0.1 \                                                                                         
  --port 8123 \                                                       
  --seed 0 \                                               
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 128 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' -ep --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE

```
```
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
--host 127.0.0.1 --port 8123 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 512 \
--random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 32 --request-rate inf --num-warmups 32 --seed 42 \
--temperature 0 --ignore-eos --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
--metric-percentiles 50,90,99 --save-result --save-detailed

```

## Details
Native heads are used on SM90 when the actual head count is 8/16/32 and the query-token count exceeds:

- SM count for 8 or 16 heads.
- Twice the SM count for 32 heads.

These are empirical performance thresholds. Each query launches one CTA, and small query batches can favor the padded kernel despite its extra head computation.

The implementation uses the actual head count, including heads gathered by DCP, and slices both queries and optional output buffers before calling FlashMLA. Existing padded workspaces remain available for fallback.

Related work and duplicate check: Reviewed open PRs matching FlashMLA small heads and SM90 sparse. #59418 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59418) adds a Triton decoder that directly reads packed FP8 KV caches, while #57673 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57673) adds an opt-in Triton backend. This PR integrates existing native BF16 kernels into the current FlashMLA sparse backend.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and preparation of this description.

 from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv
+from vllm.utils.platform_utils import num_compute_units
 from vllm.utils.torch_utils import current_stream
 from vllm.v1.attention.backend import AttentionBackend
 from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla import index_group as index_group_module
@@ -1395,6 +1396,91 @@ def test_triton_convert_rejects_req_id_longer_than_token_indices():
     torch.testing.assert_close(result, reference, rtol=0, atol=0)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("query_waves", [1, 3])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("actual_num_heads", [4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("head_size", [512, 576])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("padded_query", [False, True])
+def test_flashmla_bf16_preserves_unused_output_heads(
+    default_vllm_config,
+    dist_init,
+    workspace_init,
+    actual_num_heads,
+    head_size,
+    padded_query,
+    query_waves,
+):
+    """Only larger batches use native heads, including gathered queries."""
+    supported, reason = flashmla.is_flashmla_sparse_supported()
+    if not supported:
+        pytest.skip(reason)
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    num_tokens = query_waves * num_compute_units(
+        torch.accelerator.current_device_index()
+    )
+    impl = FlashMLASparseImpl(
+        num_heads=8,
+        head_size=head_size,
+        scale=256**-0.5,
+        num_kv_heads=1,
+        alibi_slopes=None,
+        sliding_window=None,
+        kv_cache_dtype="auto",
+        logits_soft_cap=None,
+        attn_type="decoder",
+        kv_sharing_target_layer_name=None,
+        q_lora_rank=None,
+        kv_lora_rank=512,
+        qk_nope_head_dim=256,
+        qk_rope_head_dim=head_size - 512,
+        qk_head_dim=head_size - 256,
+        v_head_dim=256,
+        kv_b_proj=ColumnParallelLinear(512, 8 * 512, bias=False),
+    )
+    gen = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0)
+    padded_heads = max(64, actual_num_heads)
+    q = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, padded_heads, head_size, generator=gen, device=device
+    ).bfloat16()
+    kv = torch.randn(128, 1, head_size, generator=gen, device=device).bfloat16()
+    indices = torch.arange(128, dtype=torch.int32, device=device).expand(
+        num_tokens, 1, -1
+    )
+    lengths = torch.tensor([1, 127, 128], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)[
+        torch.arange(num_tokens, device=device) % 3
+    ]
+    reference, _, reference_lse = flashmla.flash_mla_sparse_fwd(
+        q, kv, indices, impl.softmax_scale, topk_length=lengths
+    )
+    if not padded_query:
+        q = q[:, :actual_num_heads].contiguous()
+    out = torch.full(
+        (num_tokens, padded_heads, 512), 123.0, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
+    )
+    output, lse = impl._bf16_flash_mla_kernel(
+        q,
+        kv,
+        indices,
+        lengths,
+        actual_num_heads=actual_num_heads if padded_query else None,
+        out=out if padded_query else None,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        output, reference[:, :actual_num_heads], atol=2e-3, rtol=2e-2
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        lse, reference_lse[:, :actual_num_heads], atol=2e-4, rtol=2e-4
+    )
+    if padded_query:
+        if (
+            query_waves == 3
+            and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(90)
+            and actual_num_heads in (8, 16, 32)
+        ):
+            assert torch.all(out[:, actual_num_heads:] == 123)
+        else:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(out, reference, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
 @pytest.mark.skipif(
     torch.cuda.get_device_capability() < (9, 0),
     reason="FlashMLASparseBackend requires CUDA 9.0 or higher",

@@ -750,8 +750,9 @@ def __init__(
             **mla_args,
         )
         self.softmax_scale = scale
-        # Prefill BF16 kernel requires 64 heads on Hopper and Blackwell.
+        # Keep padded workspaces for kernels without small-head support.
         self.prefill_padding = 64
+        self._sm_count = num_compute_units(torch.accelerator.current_device_index())
         self.fp8_decode_padded_heads = self._compute_fp8_decode_padded_heads(num_heads)
 
         # The kernels read queries as wide as the cache rows. A NoPE model on
@@ -1364,6 +1365,20 @@ def _host_backed_fp8_decode(
         )
         return reshape_attn_output_for_spec_decode(output)
 
+    def _should_use_bf16_small_head_kernel(
+        self, num_tokens: int, actual_num_heads: int
+    ) -> bool:
+        if not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(90):
+            return False
+        if actual_num_heads not in (8, 16, 32):
+            return False
+
+        # Each query launches one CTA. These empirical token-per-SM cutoffs
+        # favor padding for small batches; 32 heads use a higher cutoff.
+        # They are performance heuristics, not correctness requirements.
+        min_tokens_per_sm = 2 if actual_num_heads == 32 else 1
+        return num_tokens > self._sm_count * min_tokens_per_sm
+
     def _bf16_flash_mla_kernel(
         self,
         q: torch.Tensor,
@@ -1378,17 +1393,19 @@ def _bf16_flash_mla_kernel(

         )
 
-        # NOTE(Chen): kernel requires num_local_head to be a multiple of 64.

+        # DCP can all-gather heads before this call.
         if actual_num_heads is None:
             actual_num_heads = q.shape[1]
         padded_num_heads = (
             (actual_num_heads + self.prefill_padding - 1)
             // self.prefill_padding
             * self.prefill_padding
         )
-        if q.shape[1] < padded_num_heads:
